headlineRead: The biggest new research change is not another commodity spike: it is the discovery that US data-centre power-request pipelines contain enough duplicated/speculative 'ghost demand' that regulators/utilities are forcing deposits and funding disclosure. That raises the evidence bar for AI-power demand without invalidating real physical bottlenecks. Simultaneously, August ISM Manufacturing slowed to 54.6 while Prices stayed 71.1 and electrical/electronic/memory/copper shortages remained acute. Oil/refined products and long yields strengthened together, creating a stagflationary quality split.
whatsNewNow: AI load-quality / ghost-demand moves to a top-three Developing Theme after >700 GW of US data-centre power requests triggered audits/deposit requirements.
August ISM Manufacturing is now official: 54.6 versus 55.6, with New Orders 53.7, Production 58.3, Prices 71.1 and Supplier Deliveries 59.3.
Brent settled $94.65 and WTI $90.22 after renewed US-Iran fighting; US diesel futures reached a 52-month high.
US 10Y traded near 4.80%, official Aug 31 real 10Y TIPS reached 2.44%, Japan 10Y hit 3%, and Sep Fed-hike pricing rose to roughly 68%.
Grid/OT cybersecurity is phasing in after AI-enhanced energy-system attack warnings and a sophisticated power-grid sabotage incident.
Agriculture/fertilizer outperformed on Sep 1, but CF/CTVA/BG are now less attractive to chase after moving through prior momentum/breakout levels.
whatMattersMostNow: Funded AI load quality versus speculative grid requests
Selective software/cyber rather than blanket SaaS
